{{Quote|It's not just some statue. It's important to Mandalore.|Sabine Wren describes the importance of the statue to her brother Tristan|<ref name="Art History" />}}
A '''statue of Tarre Vizsla''' was located on the [[planet]] [[Mandalore]], the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[homeworld]] of the [[Mandalorian]] people. The statue honored [[Tarre Vizsla]], an ancient [[Mandalore (title)|leader]] of Mandalore and the first Mandalorian to join the [[Jedi Order]]. The large, carved likeness of Vizsla was a symbol of hope to all Mandalorians and an acknowledgment of Mandalorian history.

During the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], the [[Occupation of Mandalore|occupying]] [[Imperial Military|Imperial forces]] took over the statue and used it as an outpost. However, in [[2 BBY]], the Mandalorians [[Sabine Wren|Sabine]] and [[Tristan Wren]] liberated the statue.

==Description==
{{Quote|So much history and hope in one carving.|Sabine Wren, to Tristan Wren|<ref name="Art History" />}}
[[File:Tarre_Vizsla.png|thumb|left|190px|Tarre Vizsla's likeness was immortalized by the statue.]]
Located in the [[desert]] region of<ref name="Art History" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]]<ref name="USWNE">''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]''</ref> [[Mandalore]],<ref name="Art History" /> the resplendently-carved statue of Tarre Vizsla stood 93 [[meter]]s (305 [[Foot|feet]]) tall.<ref name="100 objects" /> It was built in honor of [[Tarre Vizsla]],<ref name="Art History" /> the first [[Mandalorian]] ever inducted into the [[Jedi Order]] and a respected<ref name="Trials of the Darksaber">{{Rebels|Trials of the Darksaber}}</ref> former [[Mandalore (title)|leader]] of Mandalore.<ref name="Art History" /> Representing hope and history,<ref name="100 objects" /> the statue depicted Vizsla [[cloak]]ed and [[Mandalorian armor|armored]], holding the [[Darksaber]], Vizsla's famed weapon, which symbolized leadership in Mandalorian culture.<ref name="Art History" /> Notably, Vizsla did not hold the blade aloft in battle, but instead stoically pointed it at the ground, symbolically denoting the soil<ref name="100 objects" /> of the Mandalorian [[homeworld]].<ref name="USWNE" /> The larger-than-life<ref name="Wars Not Make One Great">{{GermanFanCite|104|Database}}</ref> statue was located near a main road<ref name="Art History" /> and stood for many [[Standard year|years]], visible from miles away.<ref name="100 objects" />

==History==
{{Quote|Well, you were just a baby, so you couldn't come, but Father brought me here to see the statue of Tarre Vizsla, the ancient Mandalorian ruler.|Sabine Wren, to Tristan Wren|<ref name="Art History" />}}
[[File:FODArtHistory.jpg|thumb|right|225px|Sabine and Tristan Wren discovered the Imperials had taken over the statue.]]
As a [[Youngling|child]], the Mandalorian [[Sabine Wren]] accompanied<ref name="Art History" /> her<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> [[Parent|father]], [[Alrich Wren]], to see the statue, an outing she remembered fondly for years after. During the [[Imperial Era]], the [[Galactic Empire]] constructed a [[Imperial Military|militarized]] outpost on the statue, defacing it. During a covert mission on Mandalore<ref name="Art History" /> in [[2 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> Sabine, now a [[Phoenix Cell|rebel fighter]], and her [[Clan Wren|brother]] [[Tristan Wren]] discovered [[stormtrooper]]s and Imperial fortifications built onto the statue. Sabine, personally wielding the Darksaber, joined Tristan in destroying the outpost, restoring the statue's original appearance.<ref name="Art History" />

Vizsla's statue was mentioned in "[[Mandalorians Through the Ages]]," a publication by the [[historian]] [[Eloc Throno]].<ref name="Wars Not Make One Great" /> A [[Unidentified historical book|book]] describing objects relating to [[Timeline of galactic history|galactic history]] contained an entry on the the Darksaber that mentioned the statue, elaborating on its historical significance and symbolic pose.<ref name="100 objects" /> At one point, the [[pirate]] [[Maz Kanata]] learned of Sabine and Tristan's actions and told the story of their adventure to the fellow pirate [[Hondo Ohnaka]].<ref name="FOD4">''[[Star Wars Forces of Destiny: Volume 4]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The statue of Tarre Vizsla first appeared in the [[Star Wars Forces of Destiny|''Forces of Destiny'']] animated series, debuting in "[[Art History]],"<ref name="Art History" /> the eleventh episode of the show's [[Forces of Destiny: Season Two|second season]], which was released on [[May 4]], [[2018]].<ref name="YouTube">{{DisneyYouTube|series=Star Wars Forces of Destiny|text=Art History|video=tT_p0j7znCk}}</ref>
